For every finite \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) instance with a finite experiment set \(\mathcal U\), effectively rational or real-algebraic rows, menu values, and positive costs, and a jointly realizable complete experiment menu \(\mathcal K_{\mathcal U}\ne\varnothing\), all minimum-cost Layer-3 regime-block solutions are characterized by enumerating \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\) and, for each arm, solving the finite linear feasibility problem defining \(\operatorname{PO}(S)\).  In general the elimination function \(f\) is not submodular.  In particular, there is a realizable one-domain binary one-district checked instance with two unit-cost experiments, each revealing one complete Boolean postprocessed Layer-3 output law, for which
\[
\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1\})
=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_2\})=\{\rho,\sigma\},
\qquad
\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1,e_2\})=
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.
\]
Thus the marginal gain of \(e_2\) is zero at \(S=\varnothing\) and one at \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}=\{e_1\}\), violating diminishing returns.  For this instance the exact acquisition problem is
\[
\min_{x_1,x_2\in\{0,1\}}x_1+x_2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+x_2\geq2,
\]
with unique solution \((1,1)\) and cost two; the multiplier \(y=1\) for the covering inequality certifies the matching lower bound for its continuous relaxation.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a finite checked instance satisfying the hypotheses and fix
\(S\subseteq\mathcal U\).  Joint realizability and the definition of the
subfaces give
\[
\varnothing\ne\mathcal K_{\mathcal U}\subseteq\mathcal K_S
\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\tag{1}
\]
The checked-local-arms certificate in
\(\mathrm{def:target\text{-}arm\text{-}rows}\) states, one condition at a
time, that \(\varepsilon_D>0\) and that
\(d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D\) for every
\(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\).  Hence the denominator is nonzero throughout
every subface in \((1)\).  Consequently, for every
\(q\in\mathcal K_S\) and every pair of arms \(\rho,\sigma\),
\[
Q_\rho(q)\geq Q_\sigma(q)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\frac{n_{\rho,D}^{\mathsf T}q}{d_D^{\mathsf T}q}
\geq
\frac{n_{\sigma,D}^{\mathsf T}q}{d_D^{\mathsf T}q}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(n_{\rho,D}-n_{\sigma,D})^{\mathsf T}q\geq0.
\tag{2}
\]
The second equivalence uses only multiplication by the common strictly
positive denominator.  Thus the causal conditional ranking is not being
defined by the numerator comparison; equation \((2)\) proves their equality
on the checked positive-evidence face.

By \(\mathrm{def:regime\text{-}block\text{-}acquisition}\), for a fixed
arm \(\rho\),
\[
\rho\in\operatorname{PO}(S)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists q\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}\quad
\begin{cases}
q(\omega)\geq0,&\omega\in\Omega_D,\\
A_Dq=m_D,\\
R_eq=p_e,&e\in S,\\
(n_{\rho,D}-n_{\sigma,D})^{\mathsf T}q\geq0,
&\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}.
\end{cases}
\tag{3}
\]
This is a finite linear feasibility problem.  Its feasible set is contained
in the probability simplex because the normalization row
\(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\) with value one is a row of \(A_D\).  It is
therefore bounded and closed.  If it is nonempty, it has an extreme point:
indeed, successively minimize the finitely many coordinates on the current
nonempty compact face; after the last coordinate the resulting face is a
singleton, which is an extreme point of the original polytope.  At an extreme
point, the equality rows together with some active inequality rows have full
column rank.  Otherwise a nonzero vector orthogonal to all active rows would
permit sufficiently small movements in both signs while preserving the
equalities and all inequalities, contradicting extremality.  Hence feasibility
of \((3)\) is equivalent to feasibility of at least one of the finitely many
systems obtained by declaring a full-rank subset of its inequalities active.
For each such subset, Gaussian elimination and substitution produce its unique
candidate, and exact sign tests check all remaining inequalities.  Effective
rational and real-algebraic arithmetic supplies exact equality, rank, and sign
tests, so this procedure decides \((3)\) without a limiting or numerical
tolerance argument.

There are finitely many pairs \((S,\rho)\).  Applying the preceding decision
procedure to each pair computes every \(\operatorname{PO}(S)\), including
\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U)\).  Retain
exactly those subsets for which
\(\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), sum their positive
effectively represented costs, and compare the finitely many sums exactly.
This returns all, including all ties, of the minimum-cost solutions claimed in
the first sentence of the theorem.

It remains to prove that no general submodularity claim can strengthen this
finite characterization.  Consider the one-domain binary bow graph on
\(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\) and \(Y\), with
\(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\to Y\) and
\(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\leftrightarrow Y\).  It is acyclic and has the single
district \(D=\{T_{\mathrm{tr}},Y\}\).  Both endogenous state spaces are
\(\{0,1\}\).  By
\(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}response\text{-}profile}\), a deterministic
district response profile is
\[
\omega=(t^{\mathrm{nat}},Y_0,Y_1)\in\{0,1\}^3,
\tag{4}
\]
where \(t^{\mathrm{nat}}\) is the response of the parentless treatment and
\(Y_t\) is the response of \(Y\) when \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\) is set to
\(t\).  Supply in the base menu the complete observational law
\[
P(T_{\mathrm{tr}}=0)=1,
\qquad P(T_{\mathrm{tr}}=1)=0.
\tag{5}
\]
The two raw rows from \((5)\), nonnegativity, and normalization force zero
mass on every profile with \(t^{\mathrm{nat}}=1\), and impose no restriction
on the remaining four profiles.  Write these active profiles, in order, as
\[
\omega_1=(0,0,0),\quad
\omega_2=(0,0,1),\quad
\omega_3=(0,1,0),\quad
\omega_4=(0,1,1).
\tag{6}
\]
Thus the base row face is
\(\operatorname{conv}\{\delta_{\omega_1},\delta_{\omega_2},
\delta_{\omega_3},\delta_{\omega_4}\}\).

This face is realized on the stated binary alphabets.  For any law \(q\) on
the four profiles in \((6)\), take one finite district latent block
\(U_D\sim q\), set \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}=t^{\mathrm{nat}}(U_D)\), and set
\(Y=Y_{T_{\mathrm{tr}}}(U_D)\); under intervention
\(T_{\mathrm{tr}}=t\), the latter equation returns \(Y_t(U_D)\).
The common latent block is compatible with the bidirected edge, and the last
equation is compatible with the directed edge.  There is only one domain, so
there is no cross-domain invariance condition to check.  Equivalently, every
complete supplied cell below is local to the only district and is stacked, so
the structural-separation hypothesis holds for each augmented menu; the
explicit construction gives nonemptiness, and
\(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}district\text{-}fiber\text{-}projection}\)
certifies that each displayed row face is the exact focal-saturated SCM
projection, including its boundary points.

Let the common evidence event be \(E=\top\), and declare two realizable
counterfactual arms whose favorable reward events are
\[
B_\rho=\{(Y_0,Y_1)\ne(1,1)\},
\qquad
B_\sigma=\{(Y_0,Y_1)=(1,1)\}.
\tag{7}
\]
Because there is only one district, the exhaustive locality checks accept.
On the active profiles their numerator and evidence rows are
\[
n_{\rho,D}=(1,1,1,0),\qquad
n_{\sigma,D}=(0,0,0,1),\qquad
d_D=(1,1,1,1).
\tag{8}
\]
The identity \(d_D^{\mathsf T}q=1\) on the base face proves the checked
certificate with \(\varepsilon_D=1\); in particular, no zero-denominator
case is admitted.

Let \(\mathcal U=\{e_1,e_2\}\), with \(c_{e_1}=c_{e_2}=1\).  Experiment
\(e_i\) declares the Layer-3 tuple \((Y_0,Y_1)\), applies the Boolean
postprocessor
\[
F_1=\mathbf 1\{Y_0=Y_1\},
\qquad
F_2=\mathbf 1\{(Y_0,Y_1)\ne(0,0)\},
\tag{9}
\]
and reveals its complete output law
\(P(F_i=1)=1\), \(P(F_i=0)=0\).  These are genuine counterfactual
output laws: only the Boolean pushforwards in \((9)\), not the joint law of
\((Y_0,Y_1)\), are supplied.  The output-one rows on \((6)\) are
\[
r_1=(1,0,0,1),
\qquad
r_2=(0,1,1,1),
\tag{10}
\]
and the output-zero rows are their complements.  Since normalization is
already imposed, a complement row adds exactly the complementary equation and
no further restriction.  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal K_{\varnothing}
 &=\operatorname{conv}\{\delta_{\omega_1},\delta_{\omega_2},
     \delta_{\omega_3},\delta_{\omega_4}\},\\
\mathcal K_{\{e_1\}}
 &=\operatorname{conv}\{\delta_{\omega_1},\delta_{\omega_4}\},\\
\mathcal K_{\{e_2\}}
 &=\operatorname{conv}\{\delta_{\omega_2},\delta_{\omega_3},
     \delta_{\omega_4}\},\\
\mathcal K_{\{e_1,e_2\}}
 &=\{\delta_{\omega_4}\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
The last point mass realizes the complete laws of both experiments, so the
whole experiment menu is jointly realizable.  Equations \((8)\) and \((11)\)
show that each of \(\delta_{\omega_1},\delta_{\omega_2},
\delta_{\omega_3}\) makes \(\rho\) uniquely optimal, whereas
\(\delta_{\omega_4}\) makes \(\sigma\) uniquely optimal.  Since there are
exactly two arms,
\[
\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=
\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1\})=
\operatorname{PO}(\{e_2\})=\{\rho,\sigma\},
\qquad
\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1,e_2\})=
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.
\tag{12}
\]
It follows from the definition of \(f\) that
\[
f(\{e_2\})-f(\varnothing)=0
<1=f(\{e_1,e_2\})-f(\{e_1\}).
\tag{13}
\]
Taking \(S=\varnothing\),
\(T_{\mathrm{exp}}=\{e_1\}\), and \(e=e_2\), equation \((13)\)
contradicts the diminishing-returns inequality required for submodularity.

Finally, \((12)\) shows that a selected set preserves the full-information
possibly-optimal set if and only if it contains both experiments.  With
\(x_i=\mathbf 1\{e_i\in S\}\), the exact acquisition problem is therefore
\[
\min_{x_1,x_2\in\{0,1\}}x_1+x_2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+x_2\geq2.
\tag{14}
\]
Its only feasible binary point is \((1,1)\), of cost two.  In the continuous
relaxation \(0\leq x_i\leq1\), the nonnegative multiplier \(y=1\) on the
covering inequality gives the lower bound
\(x_1+x_2\geq2y=2\), and \((1,1)\) attains it.  This proves the claimed
matching certificate and completes the construction.

statements.statement: Fix \(s\in\mathcal S\setminus\{\star\}\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(0<|D\cap\Delta_s|<|D|\).  Omit district closure, retain recursive compatibility, district factorization, and district-kernel invariance exactly as stated, and restrict the available information to the complete laws supplied from this designated partially selected source \(s\).  For a scalar row \(\ell\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}\), its target value is universally determined by those source laws if and only if \(\ell\) is constant on \(\Omega_D\).  More strongly, every nonconstant \(\ell\) admits two finite source-labelled SCM families on the original declared alphabets \(\mathcal X\) that satisfy all retained assumptions, induce identical complete supplied laws in domain \(s\), and have unequal target values of \(\ell\).  If one additionally requires invariance of the marginal response law on \(I=D\setminus\Delta_s\), then universal transport holds if and only if \(\ell\) is constant on every fiber of the coordinate projection \(\pi_I:\Omega_D\to\pi_I(\Omega_D)\).  For every finite real matrix, componentwise universal transport holds if and only if every row has the corresponding constancy property.  For rational rows, and for real-algebraic rows given by effective representations supporting exact equality comparison, the criterion is decidable by finite enumeration; failure returns a row index and two response profiles giving an original-alphabet two-Dirac certificate.  Thus binary incidence and event rows, \(\{-1,0,1\}\)-valued arm-gap rows, finite real reward rows, and linear-certificate rows are all covered.  The result is only a designated-source-information limitation: it makes no claim after adding target-domain data or data from a wholly unselected source whose district law is tied to the target.
statements.proof_tex:
Put
\[
J=D\cap\Delta_s,
\qquad
I=D\setminus\Delta_s.
\]
The displayed hypothesis gives \(J\ne\varnothing\), \(I\ne\varnothing\), and \(D\cap\Delta_s\ne\varnothing\).  Consequently the antecedent \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) in Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}kernel\text{-}invariance}\) is false for the designated pair \((s,D)\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:recursive\text{-}compatibility}\) constrains each domain separately, and Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\) constrains distinct districts within one domain; neither of them equates the focal district response laws in domains \(s\) and \(\star\).  These observations use exactly the retained assumptions after district closure is omitted.

For a row \(\ell:\Omega_D\to\mathbb R\) and a probability vector \(q\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\), define the finite pairing
\[
\langle\ell,q\rangle
=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_D}\ell(\omega)q(\omega).
\tag{1}
\]
Suppose first that \(\ell\) is nonconstant.  Finiteness of \(\Omega_D\), supplied by Definition \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}response\text{-}profile}\), gives profiles \(\omega_0,\omega_1\in\Omega_D\) for which
\[
\alpha:=\ell(\omega_0)\ne\ell(\omega_1)=:\beta.
\tag{2}
\]
For \(i\in\{0,1\}\), prescribe the focal district laws of a source-labelled family \(\mathbf M^{(i)}\) by
\[
q_D^{s,(i)}=\delta_{\omega_0},
\qquad
q_D^{\star,(i)}=\delta_{\omega_i},
\tag{3}
\]
where \(\delta_\omega\) is the point mass at \(\omega\).  For every \(t\in\mathcal S\setminus\{s,\star\}\), put
\[
q_D^{t,(i)}=
\begin{cases}
\delta_{\omega_i},&D\cap\Delta_t=\varnothing,\\
\delta_{\omega_0},&D\cap\Delta_t\ne\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\tag{4}
\]
Thus, whenever the antecedent of district-kernel invariance is true for \((t,D)\), equation (4) makes the source law equal to the target law in that same family.  For every district \(D'\ne D\), the nonemptiness of each declared alphabet supplies a tuple of constant response maps and hence an element of \(\Omega_{D'}\).  Choose one such profile \(\bar\omega_{D'}\in\Omega_{D'}\) and set
\[
q_{D'}^{t,(i)}=\delta_{\bar\omega_{D'}}
\quad
\text{for every }t\in\mathcal S\text{ and }i\in\{0,1\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Equation (5) satisfies every remaining instance of district-kernel invariance.

We next verify original-alphabet realization rather than merely prescribing formal probability vectors.  By Definition \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}response\text{-}profile}\), each \(\omega\in\Omega_D\) already consists of deterministic response maps with codomain \(\mathcal X_V\) at every graph-allowed parent configuration, and the same is true of each \(\bar\omega_{D'}\).  In each domain, use the indicated deterministic tables as the structural equations and equip their exogenous inputs with point-mass laws.  A point mass factors across any partition, so the exogenous response blocks of distinct districts are independent, as required by Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\).  Every table uses only graph-allowed parents and values in the declared alphabet.  Since \(G\) is acyclic, recursive evaluation in a topological order is unique.  Hence the constructed models are finite recursive SCMs compatible with \(G\) on the original \(\mathcal X\), which verifies Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:recursive\text{-}compatibility}\).  Equations (3)--(5) verify every true-antecedent instance of Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}kernel\text{-}invariance}\).  No observed state has been added.

All district tables and laws in the designated source are the same for \(i=0\) and \(i=1\): the focal source law is \(\delta_{\omega_0}\) by (3), and every nonfocal law is common by (5).  Therefore
\[
M^{s,(0)}=M^{s,(1)}.
\tag{6}
\]
Every observational, interventional, or declared same-source Layer-3 output is a deterministic recursive evaluation followed by marginalization under this source SCM.  Equation (6) therefore implies equality of all complete laws supplied from domain \(s\), not merely equality of one reported row.  In particular,
\[
\langle\ell,q_D^{s,(0)}\rangle
=\langle\ell,q_D^{s,(1)}\rangle
=\alpha.
\tag{7}
\]
The target values, however, are
\[
\langle\ell,q_D^{\star,(0)}\rangle=\alpha,
\qquad
\langle\ell,q_D^{\star,(1)}\rangle=\beta,
\tag{8}
\]
and they differ by (2).  Equations (3)--(8) are the promised equal-source-law, unequal-target, original-alphabet certificate for every nonconstant real row.

Conversely, if \(\ell\equiv c\) on \(\Omega_D\), normalization of every \(q\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\) gives
\[
\langle\ell,q\rangle
=c\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_D}q(\omega)
=c.
\tag{9}
\]
Thus the target value of a constant row is known without any cross-domain information.  Equations (2)--(8) exclude universal source-only determination for every other row, while (9) proves it for constant rows.  This proves the first equivalence.  Notice that the pair is allowed to differ in a target-domain law and in a further source law whose unselected focal district must equal the target.  Accordingly, the conclusion concerns only information supplied from the designated partially selected source; it does not survive automatically if either kind of extra law is observed.

Now add the premise that the response-profile marginal on \(I\) is invariant between the designated source and target.  Let
\[
\pi_I:\Omega_D\longrightarrow\pi_I(\Omega_D)
\]
be coordinate restriction to the response maps of vertices in \(I\).  The added premise is the finite pushforward equality
\[
(\pi_I)_{\#}q_D^s=(\pi_I)_{\#}q_D^\star.
\tag{10}
\]
Suppose that \(\ell\) is constant on every fiber of \(\pi_I\).  Then the function
\[
\widetilde\ell(u)=\ell(\omega)
\quad\text{for any }\omega\text{ with }\pi_I(\omega)=u
\tag{11}
\]
is well defined on \(\pi_I(\Omega_D)\), and \(\ell=\widetilde\ell\circ\pi_I\).  Grouping finite sums by projection fibers and using (10) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\langle\ell,q_D^s\rangle
&=\sum_{u\in\pi_I(\Omega_D)}
  \widetilde\ell(u)(\pi_I)_{\#}q_D^s(u)\\
&=\sum_{u\in\pi_I(\Omega_D)}
  \widetilde\ell(u)(\pi_I)_{\#}q_D^\star(u)\\
&=\langle\ell,q_D^\star\rangle.
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
Hence fiber constancy is sufficient.

For necessity, suppose that fiber constancy fails.  There are then \(\omega_0,\omega_1\in\Omega_D\) such that
\[
\pi_I(\omega_0)=\pi_I(\omega_1),
\qquad
\ell(\omega_0)\ne\ell(\omega_1).
\tag{13}
\]
Repeat the construction (3)--(6) with this pair.  In the model \(\mathbf M^{(i)}\), the source and target pushforwards are respectively
\[
(\pi_I)_{\#}\delta_{\omega_0}
=\delta_{\pi_I(\omega_0)}
=\delta_{\pi_I(\omega_1)}
=(\pi_I)_{\#}\delta_{\omega_i}.
\tag{14}
\]
Thus each model satisfies the added marginal-invariance premise (10), the two models still have identical complete laws in source \(s\), and their target row values differ by (13).  This proves necessity and the second scalar equivalence.

Let \(L\in\mathbb R^{k\times|\Omega_D|}\) be any finite matrix with row functions \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k\), and define
\[
Lq=
\bigl(\langle\ell_1,q\rangle,\ldots,
      \langle\ell_k,q\rangle\bigr)^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{15}
\]
If every row is fiber-constant, equation (12), applied separately to each \(\ell_j\), gives \(Lq_D^s=Lq_D^\star\).  If some row \(\ell_j\) is not fiber-constant, choose a failing pair for that row and apply (13)--(14); the \(j\)-th target components then differ although the complete designated-source laws agree.  This proves the componentwise matrix equivalence under (10).  Without (10), the same argument uses (2)--(9) and shows that componentwise universal transport is equivalent to every row being constant on all of \(\Omega_D\).

The characterizations are finite algorithms.  Under (10), enumerate, for each row \(j\), all pairs \((\omega,\omega')\in\Omega_D^2\) satisfying \(\pi_I(\omega)=\pi_I(\omega')\), and compare \(\ell_j(\omega)\) with \(\ell_j(\omega')\).  Without (10), enumerate all pairs.  This uses at most \(k|\Omega_D|^2\) equality comparisons.  Rational equality is decided exactly by integer cross multiplication after choosing fraction representations.  For an effectively represented real-algebraic entry, exact equality comparison is part of the stipulated effective representation, so the same finite loop is exact.  Exhaustion without a failure certifies the required constancy.  A failure returns \((j,\omega_0,\omega_1)\), and equations (3)--(8), or (3)--(8) together with (14), construct the two-Dirac certificate.  This is the finite leakage test named by Definition \(\mathrm{def:partial\text{-}district\text{-}leakage\text{-}handle}\).

By Definition \(\mathrm{def:incidence\text{-}row}\), binary event cells are scalar rows and hence are a direct special case.  Rows with entries in \(\{-1,0,1\}\), including pairwise arm gaps, arbitrary real-valued reward rows on the finite profile set, and rows used in finite linear certificates are also scalar rows in \(\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}\); the proved equivalences therefore apply to them without alteration.

As the smallest exact stress check, take binary vertices \(X\) and \(Y\) with ADMG \(X\leftrightarrow Y\), let \(D=\{X,Y\}\), and let \(\Delta_s=\{X\}\).  Choose constant response profiles \(\omega_0=(X=0,Y=0)\) and \(\omega_1=(X=1,Y=0)\), and take \(\ell(\omega)=\mathbf 1\{X(\omega)=1\}\).  The two source laws are both \(\delta_{\omega_0}\), whereas the target laws \(\delta_{\omega_0}\) and \(\delta_{\omega_1}\) give exact target values zero and one.  Their \(I=\{Y\}\) marginals are identical, so the same pair also witnesses the fiber criterion.  Restoring district closure excludes this selection pattern because neither \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) nor \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) holds.  This verifies on the smallest two-profile instance that the omitted condition is load-bearing.  No division, conditioning, positivity premise, or limiting argument is used anywhere in the proof.

statements.statement:
There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
If \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, the one-district fiber-projection theorem gives the exact local equality
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D),
\]
and \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) itself entails a nonempty focal-district-saturated compatibility fiber. This equality requires saturation only of the focal district and preserves the graph-compatible restrictions of every \(D'\ne D\). Cross-district coupling of a complete supplied cell is harmless for the fixed-baseline replacement exactly when its baseline-averaged focal row lies in \(R_D(m_D)\), because
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^{\perp}.
\]
Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and hence with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), is a baseline-free sufficient certificate for this equality. The baseline-averaged predicate is generally baseline-dependent and not directly checkable from menu cells alone; allowing a different baseline for each candidate \(q\) is not asserted. Outside focal-district saturation and baseline-averaged separation, \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is certified only as an outer relaxation. This local equality is distinct from the first, all-district-saturated global row, whose Cartesian district variation makes the multi-affine program exact. Consequently a failed local face test is not a global nonidentification certificate outside the focal projection theorem's scope; distinct endpoint optimizers of the appropriate exact global program are the paired-model certificate whenever their objective values differ.
statements.justification: The theorem separates exact all-district multi-affine variation, exact sparse canonical optimization, and exact single-baseline focal-district geometry.
statements.gap: Global programs retain every cross-district polynomial equality; locally, a weaker baseline-averaged condition preserves those cells than pointwise active-slice control.
statements.consumer: Global bounds and pruning use exact endpoint optimizers, while local LP certificates use focal saturation plus baseline-averaged separation or its baseline-free sufficient checks.
statements.proof_tex:
For a saturated compatible family, Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:recursive\text{-}compatibility}\), together with finite total probability, give for every cell \(C\)
\[
P_{M^s}(C)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_D\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1_C(\omega)\prod_Dq_D^s(\omega_D)
=\Psi_C^s(\theta^s).
\tag{1}
\]
For a supplied postprocessed output cell, Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:typed\text{-}menu\text{-}realizability}\) gives directly
\[
P_a^s(y)=\mathcal L_{M^s}(f_a(T_a))(y)
=P_{M^s}\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\tag{2}
\]
The deterministic preimage identity evaluates the indicator in \((1)\); it does not introduce unsupplied tuple-cell probabilities.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}kernel\text{-}invariance}\) supplies every equality \(q_D^s=q_D^\star\) required when \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), while district closure ensures that the declared unchanged or changed status concerns the whole district.  Hence the response-law tuple induced by any family in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\) belongs to \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\).

Conversely, let \(\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\).  For each \((s,D)\), take one finite latent block with state space \(\Omega_D\) and law \(q_D^s\); make the blocks independent across original districts, and let every structural equation read its stored deterministic response map.  The state spaces remain exactly \(\mathcal X\), and acyclicity gives a unique recursive evaluation.  The second line of \((2)\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def:exact\text{-}global\text{-}canonical\text{-}fiber}\) enforces every unchanged-district equality, and its last line plus \((2)\) enforces every supplied complete output law.  Thus the constructed family lies in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\), and \((1)\) gives all target cells simultaneously.  This proves the first joint range equality.  Each summand of \((1)\) contains at most one coordinate from each visited original-district law, so \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine and has total degree no larger than the number of visited districts.

For arbitrary \(G\), apply Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}canonical\text{-}counterfactual\text{-}equivalence}\) in every domain to the finite family of all complete response-table counterfactuals, all supplied cells, and all cells in \(\mathcal F\).  Use the response-type encoding itself, so the same encoding map is used for a source and target district whose response-block laws agree.  The resulting canonical family preserves every supplied and target joint counterfactual law and every required unchanged-district response-law equality.  It therefore determines a point of \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\).  Conversely, each point of that fiber consists of one-hot recursive structural tables, canonical exogenous probability vectors, every graph-compatible within-district restriction, independence across original districts, the required cross-domain response-law equalities, and every supplied complete-cell equation.  Reading those coordinates as an SCM family therefore gives an element of \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) on the original alphabets.  Recursive evaluation gives \(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^s\), proving the sparse canonical joint range equality.

Each parameter fiber is a closed subset of a finite product of compact probability simplices and finite one-hot table sets, hence compact.  Its defining constraints are polynomial equalities and inequalities, so it is semialgebraic.  The relevant compatibility hypothesis makes it nonempty.  Fix either exact row \((\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)\) in the statement.  Every target-cell polynomial is continuous, so it attains its minimum and maximum on \(\Lambda\).  Joint range equality makes these extrema the sharp causal bounds and turns their optimizers into original-alphabet compatible endpoint models.  Equality of the extrema is equivalent to constancy of the cell on the fiber, hence to identification.  If they differ, the two endpoint models differ in target value.  Since every cell probability lies in \([0,1]\), at least one endpoint strictly improves its logical bound exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one.  No connectedness has been assumed, so no interval-filling conclusion follows.

Apply the same reasoning to the nonnegative evidence polynomial.  Compactness gives attained values
\[
e_-=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
e_+=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
The exhaustive cases are
\[
e_+=0,\qquad e_-=0<e_+,\qquad e_->0.
\tag{3}
\]
They respectively mean uniform zero evidence, coexistence of zero- and positive-evidence compatible models, and uniform strict positivity.  Division on the whole fiber is valid only in the third case.  There the conditional ratio is continuous on compact \(\Lambda\), and hence attains the stated sharp lower and upper bounds.  Furthermore
\[
Q_\sigma^\star-Q_\rho^\star
=\frac{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star-
\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star}{\Xi_E^\star}.
\tag{4}
\]
Because the denominator in \((4)\) is positive, the sign is exactly the sign of the numerator gap.  A continuous gap that is positive at every point of compact \(\Lambda\) has positive minimum, and the converse is immediate.  Likewise, opposite strict rankings exist exactly when its attained minimum is negative and its attained maximum is positive.  This proves the pruning claims.

Finally, Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:district\text{-}cell\text{-}linearity}\) places every broad compatible focal law in \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\).  The exact focal equality, the identity
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^{\perp},
\]
the fixed-baseline preservation calculation, and the asserted boundary realization are precisely Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}district\text{-}fiber\text{-}projection}\).  Lemmas \(\mathrm{lem:active\text{-}slice\text{-}implies\text{-}baseline\text{-}averaged}\) and \(\mathrm{lem:structural\text{-}separation\text{-}implies\text{-}active\text{-}slice}\) give the two baseline-free sufficient conditions.  These arguments preserve every cross-district polynomial equation in the global fibers; they do not identify the broad projection with the row face without the focal theorem's hypotheses.  Thus only unequal optimizers of an exact global program, or a local face witness under the exact focal projection theorem, supply the asserted paired-model certificate.

Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{r\times N}\), \(m\in\mathbb R^r\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^N\). If \(K=\{q\in\mathbb R^N:q\geq0,\ Aq=m\}\) is nonempty and bounded, then both optima are attained and

source.verbatim_statement: Let P \(\subset R[X^{[1]},\ldots,X^{[\omega]},Y]_{\le d}\) be a finite set of s polynomials, where \(X^{[i]}\) is a block of \(k_i\) variables, and Y is a block of \(\ell\) variables. Consider the quantified formula \(\Psi(Y)=(Q_1X^{[1]})\cdots(Q_\omega X^{[\omega]})\Phi(X^{[1]},\ldots,X^{[\omega]},Y)\), where \(\Phi\) is a quantifier-free P-formula. Then there exists a quantifier-free formula \(\Theta(Y)=\bigvee_{i=1}^{I}\bigwedge_{j=1}^{J_i}\bigvee_{n=1}^{N_{ij}}\operatorname{sign}(P_{ijn}(Y))=\sigma_{ijn}\) equivalent to \(\Psi\), where \(P_{ijn}(Y)\) are polynomials in the variables Y and \(\sigma_{ijn}\in\{-1,0,1\}\). Furthermore, \(I\le s^{(k_\omega+1)\cdots(k_1+1)(\ell+1)}d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)O(\ell)}\), \(J_i\le s^{(k_\omega+1)\cdots(k_1+1)}d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)}\), \(N_{ij}\le d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)}\), and the degrees of the polynomials \(P_{ijn}(y)\) are bounded by \(d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)}\). Moreover, there exists an algorithm ([5, Algorithm 14.5] (Quantifier Elimination)) to compute \(\Theta(Y)\) with complexity \(s^{(k_\omega+1)\cdots(k_1+1)(\ell+1)}d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)O(\ell)}\) in D, where D denotes the ring generated by the coefficients of the polynomials in P. If D = Z and \(\tau\) denotes an upper bound on bitsizes of P, then the bitsizes of the integers in the intermediate computations and the output are bounded by \(\tau d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)O(\ell)}\).

statements.statement:
For every district \(D\),
\[
\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\Longrightarrow\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P).
\]
The implication is strict in general.  In particular, take two independent binary response coordinates \(Y_0\) and \(Z\) generated by distinct singleton districts, let \(D\) be the district generating \(Y_0\), and supply in the target domain both the complete marginal law of \(Y_0\) and the complete joint law of \((Y_0,Z)\).  The resulting menu satisfies \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) but not \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\).
statements.proof_tex:
Assume \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\).  If a complete supplied output-cell indicator is independent of \(\omega_D\), then every focal slice is either the zero row or the normalization row.  If it depends only on \(\omega_D\), then every slice is its accepted raw row.  For a deterministic postprocessor this conclusion follows by evaluating its finite preimage indicator, not by adding tuple-cell probabilities to the menu.  In both cases every slice belongs to \(R_D(m_D)\), proving \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\).

For strictness, let \(Y_0\) and \(Z\) be independent binary response coordinates in distinct singleton districts, let \(D\) generate \(Y_0\), and supply in the target domain the complete marginal law of \(Y_0\) and the complete joint law of \((Y_0,Z)\).  Write
\[
h_y(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{Y_0=y\},
\qquad
k_z(\omega_{-D})=\mathbf 1\{Z=z\}.
\]
The marginal menu retains \(h_y\), whereas a joint cell has cross-district indicator \(h_yk_z\), so structural separation fails.  After fixing \(\omega_{-D}\), however, its focal slice is either zero or \(h_y\), both in the active row space.  Hence active-slice separation holds.  Independent Bernoulli response blocks realize this menu on the original binary alphabets, proving strictness.

statements.statement:
For every district \(D\),
\[
\bigl\{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing
\text{ and }\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
\Longrightarrow \mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P).
\]
Together with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\Longrightarrow\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), this gives the convenient hierarchy
\[
\bigl\{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing
\text{ and }\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
\Longrightarrow
\bigl\{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing
\text{ and }\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
\Longrightarrow \mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P).
\]
The second implication is strict on finite original alphabets: there is a three-vertex binary DAG and a complete target-domain menu for which \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds but \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) fails because two Boolean focal slices outside \(R_D(m_D)\) average to a row inside it under the witnessing nonfocal product law.
statements.justification: This hierarchy makes the sharp single-baseline preservation premise explicit while retaining two increasingly simple sufficient checks.
statements.gap: Pointwise active-slice control is stronger than the fixed-baseline construction needs because only averages under the frozen nonfocal product law enter complete-cell probabilities.
statements.consumer: The focal projection theorem and its identification, dominance, frontier, and global corollaries use baseline-averaged separation for exact lifting.
statements.proof_tex:
Choose \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\).  District factorization gives the finite nonfocal product law \(\nu_{-D}^{0,s}\).  Under \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), every focal slice lies in the linear space \(R_D(m_D)\), so
\[
\bar\chi_C^{s,\mathbf M^0}
=\sum_{\omega_{-D}}
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
\chi_{C,\omega_{-D}}
\in R_D(m_D).
\tag{1}
\]
The same baseline works for every cell and domain, proving \(\mathsf{BASep}_D\).  Composition with the structural-separation lemma gives the full hierarchy.

For strictness, take independent fair binary roots \(X,Z\) feeding the deterministic binary child \(Y=\mathbf 1\{X=Z\}\), and let \(D=\{X\}\).  Supply only the complete target-domain output law of \(Y\).  Then \(A_D=\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\) and
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{span}\{(1,1)\}.
\]
The two focal slices of \(\{Y=1\}\) are \((1,0)\) and \((0,1)\), so active-slice separation fails.  Their average under the fair nonfocal law of \(Z\) is \((1/2,1/2)\in R_D(m_D)\); the complementary output cell is analogous.  Focal saturation permits every law of \(X\) while the fair law of \(Z\) and the structural table of \(Y\) stay fixed, so this single compatible baseline proves \(\mathsf{BASep}_D\).  Thus the second implication is strict on the original binary alphabets.

statements.statement: Assume \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and every supplied output-cell probability is effectively rational or real algebraic.  Let \(\mathbb D\) be the effective ordered coefficient ring they generate, with its effective embedding into \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) for coefficient representation and exact arithmetic.  The \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) outputs of \(\mathsf{DCTFTR\text{-}CAN}\) are equivalent to their defining first-order formulas in every real-closed field extension containing \(\mathbb D\), and in particular their realizations over the ordinary real field \(\mathbb R\) are used for the causal conclusions.  For either an unconditional finite target-domain counterfactual cell \(T\) or the conditional query \(Q_\rho^\star=P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\mid E)\), the algorithm terminates and returns a \(\mathsf{HybridResult}\).  A fast-path \(\operatorname{ID\_RAT}(F,\delta)\) has \(F\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) and equals the causal query throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  Otherwise, for the real canonical fiber \(S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\), the fallback returns quantifier-free formulas whose real realizations are exactly the full target range and its attained lower and upper endpoints, together with an exact singleton decision.  For an unconditional target it returns \(\operatorname{UNCOND\_QE}\), and identification holds exactly when the real range is a singleton.  For a conditional target it evaluates the closed sentences \(\mathsf Z\), \(\mathsf N\), and \(\mathsf P\) from \(\mathrm{def:hybrid\text{-}result\text{-}grammar}\): it returns the payload-free terminal \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE\_QE}\) exactly under \(\mathsf Z\), the payload-free terminal \(\operatorname{NOT\_UNIFORMLY\_DEFINED\_QE}\) exactly under \(\mathsf N\), and only under \(\mathsf P\) forms the conditional real range and returns \(\operatorname{COND\_QE}\).  In the last case evidence is uniformly positive on \(S\), and identification holds exactly when the conditional real range is a singleton.  Exact operations in \(\mathbb D\) compute the output syntax and evaluate every closed quantifier-free decision.  A non-singleton real range implies, by exact canonical range equivalence, two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families with unequal target values; the algorithm is not claimed to output endpoint values, algebraic samples, canonical parameters, or paired SCMs.  A local face failure alone is never used as broad-model nonidentification, and no claim is made that all real range points are algebraic.
statements.justification: This is the fixed-declared-alphabet completeness result: every unresolved local trace is completed by an exact identified value, a zero or nonuniform evidence certificate, or two same-menu original-alphabet SCMs.
statements.gap: CTFTR treats heterogeneous Layer-1/2 transport, CTFIDU+ treats one-specification Layer-3 identification, and canonical bounding work does not provide this source-labelled fast-path-plus-exact-fallback transport certificate.
statements.consumer: A user receives either an allowed rational formula or a checkable global algebraic certificate and explicit canonical endpoint models, with division rejected unless evidence is uniformly positive.
statements.proof_tex:
Run \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) first.  By Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:recursion\text{-}soundness}\), the run terminates uniquely.  If it returns an identifying expression \(F\), that theorem gives
\[
F(\mathcal P)=P_{M^\star}(T)
\quad\text{or}\quad
F(\mathcal P)=P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\mid E)
\tag{1}
\]
for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), with every quotient protected by its stored certificate.  Definition \(\mathrm{def:allowed\text{-}rational\text{-}functional}\) gives \(F\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\), proving the fast-path clause.  Every other local terminal invokes the canonical phase.

Put
\[
S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathbb R^N.
\tag{2}
\]
The nonemptiness hypothesis and Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:exact\text{-}global\text{-}canonical\text{-}frontier}\) imply that \(S\) is nonempty, compact, and real semialgebraic, and that its joint target-cell ranges equal those over the broad original-alphabet compatibility fiber.  Let \(\mathbb D\) be the effective ordered coefficient ring generated by the supplied rational or real-algebraic output probabilities.  Its stipulated presentations give exact arithmetic and signs, and its ordered embedding into \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) supplies exact coefficient representations without restricting the variables in \((2)\).

Fix a real-closed field \(K\) containing an ordered copy of \(\mathbb D\).  Apply Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:basu\text{-}mohammad\text{-}nezhad\text{-}quantifier\text{-}elimination}\) with ambient field \(K\).  Its algorithm terminates and uses only arithmetic in the coefficient ring.  The deterministic output is therefore one \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) syntax whose interpretation is equivalent to the input in every such \(K\).  In particular this holds for \(K=\mathbb R\), so arbitrary real canonical probabilities and real target values are retained.

For an unconditional target write \(p_T=\Phi_{T,\mathrm{can}}^\star\).  Quantifier elimination applied to
\[
\varphi_T(t)=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge t-p_T(x)=0]
\tag{3}
\]
returns \(\chi_T\) satisfying, for every \(t\in\mathbb R\),
\[
\chi_T(t)\Longleftrightarrow
\exists x\in S\;t=p_T(x)
\Longleftrightarrow
\exists\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\;
t=P_{M^\star}(T),
\tag{4}
\]
where the second equivalence is the exact global joint range theorem.  Eliminating the closed non-singleton sentence therefore decides identification exactly.  Compactness of \(S\) and continuity of \(p_T\) give an attained minimum \(\ell_T\) and maximum \(u_T\).  Hence
\[
\chi_T(\ell)\wedge\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow\ell\leq t]
\tag{5}
\]
holds over \(\mathbb R\) exactly when \(\ell=\ell_T\); attainment gives existence and antisymmetry gives uniqueness.  The reversed inequality similarly defines \(u_T\).  Quantifier elimination preserves these real equivalences, without requiring either endpoint or every range point to be algebraic.

For a conditional target let
\[
e(x)=\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(x),
\qquad
n(x)=\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(x).
\tag{6}
\]
Causal probability semantics gives \(e(x)\geq0\) on the nonempty set \(S\).  Exactly one of
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\mathsf Z:&\neg\exists x\in S\;e(x)>0,\\
\mathsf N:&(\exists x\in S\;e(x)=0)\wedge(\exists x\in S\;e(x)>0),\\
\mathsf P:&\neg\exists x\in S\;e(x)=0
\end{array}
\tag{7}
\]
holds.  Uniform quantifier elimination and exact evaluation of the three closed outputs therefore give the claimed payload-free statuses.  Under \(\mathsf Z\), evidence is zero throughout.  Under \(\mathsf N\), the conditional is undefined at one compatible law and defined at another, so division on the whole fiber is rejected.  Under \(\mathsf P\), continuity and compactness give
\[
\min_{x\in S}e(x)>0.
\tag{8}
\]
Only then is \(e(x)t-n(x)=0\) equivalent to \(t=n(x)/e(x)\).  Consequently the real realization of
\[
\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0\wedge e(x)t-n(x)=0]
\tag{9}
\]
is exactly the conditional causal range.  The ratio is continuous by \((8)\), so the compactness argument for \((5)\) gives its attained real endpoints and the closed non-singleton sentence gives its exact singleton decision.

Only finitely many calls to the cited terminating procedure occur, proving termination.  If either real range is non-singleton, two distinct attained values exist; the exact-global joint range theorem supplies two original-alphabet same-menu compatible SCM families realizing them.  This is an existential consequence, not algorithmic witness extraction.  The procedure returns no cylindrical decomposition trace, sample, isolating datum, explicit endpoint value, canonical parameter, or paired SCM, and no step restricts the causal realization to algebraic points.

statements.statement: Every finite fixing trace accepted by the extraction calculus preserves the represented event probability.  More precisely, if the trace expands its input and output into finite response-profile expressions, uses division only by a separately certified positive context probability, and its exact checker verifies the cleared-denominator polynomial identity, then the input and output expressions agree in every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix an accepted finite fixing trace \(\tau\), fix a domain label \(s\) occurring in the trace, and fix \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). By \(\mathrm{def:compatibility\text{-}fiber}\), the family \(\mathbf M\) satisfies \(\mathrm{ass:recursive\text{-}compatibility}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\). Acyclicity and the finite response carrier of \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}response\text{-}profile}\) imply that recursive substitution assigns to every event \(A\) occurring in the trace a total deterministic indicator
\[
 I_A:\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D\longrightarrow\{0,1\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The vertex set, its district partition, every declared state space, and every response-profile set are finite; hence the product and every sum below are finite. Independence of the district response blocks, which is \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\), gives
\[
 P_{M^s}(A)
 =\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
 I_A(\omega)\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^s(\omega_D).
\tag{2}
\]
Thus each unconditional response-profile event probability is a polynomial with integer coefficients in the finitely many coordinates \(q_D^s(\omega_D)\). The same argument applies separately to every source-labelled probability leaf. Algebraic combinations of leaves are therefore polynomials in the union of their coordinate families; this observation does not posit any joint probability law across distinct domain labels.

We first justify every strict-positivity certificate that can guard a divisor in \(\tau\). Let \(x\) collect the finitely many response-law coordinates named by such a certificate. The typing rules of \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\) require its declared compatibility fiber to be represented by checked constraints
\[
 h_i(x)=0\quad(1\le i\le r),
 \qquad
 g_j(x)\ge 0\quad(1\le j\le t),
\tag{3}
\]
and require the response coordinates of every model in that fiber to satisfy these constraints. For a rational-constant certificate, exact normalization verifies a rational lower bound \(\varepsilon>0\) for the certified polynomial \(p\). For a linear face certificate, the checker verifies rational multipliers and the polynomial identity
\[
 p(x)-\varepsilon
 =\sum_{i=1}^{r}\alpha_i h_i(x)
  +\sum_{j=1}^{t}\lambda_j g_j(x),
 \qquad \varepsilon>0,\quad \lambda_j\ge 0.
\tag{4}
\]
For a preordering certificate, it verifies
\[
 p(x)-\varepsilon
 =\sum_{i=1}^{r}\tau_i(x)h_i(x)
  +\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}
    \sigma_J(x)\prod_{j\in J}g_j(x),
 \qquad \varepsilon>0,
\tag{5}
\]
where every displayed \(\sigma_J\) is exactly checked to be a finite sum of squares of rational polynomials. Substitution of (3) into (4) gives \(p(x)\ge\varepsilon>0\). In (5), the equality terms vanish, each factor \(g_j(x)\) is nonnegative, every finite product of those factors is nonnegative, and every \(\sigma_J(x)\) is nonnegative; hence again \(p(x)\ge\varepsilon>0\). The rational-constant case has the same conclusion by its exact comparison. These cases exhaust the positivity constructors in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\). Consequently every context probability used as a divisor by the accepted trace is strictly positive at \(\mathbf M\).

We next verify the probability constructors. The false and true events have indicators zero and one. For a finite pairwise-disjoint family \((A_j:j\in J)\), pointwise equality of indicators gives
\[
 I_{\bigsqcup_{j\in J}A_j}=\sum_{j\in J}I_{A_j},
\]
and substitution in (2) yields
\[
 P_{M^s}\!\left(\bigsqcup_{j\in J}A_j\right)
 =\sum_{j\in J}P_{M^s}(A_j).
\tag{6}
\]
Marginalization is (6) applied to the finite partition indexed by the marginalized variable's declared state space. Pointwise \(I_{A^{\mathsf c}}=1-I_A\), so normalization of (2) gives
\[
 P_{M^s}(A^{\mathsf c})=1-P_{M^s}(A).
\tag{7}
\]
An algebraic product constructor preserves equality of already interpreted scalar expressions. If a product is annotated as the probability of a district-split event, its annotation is valid because \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\) makes the indicated district response blocks independent. A type-correct substitution is a homomorphism for rational constants, finite sums, differences, and products, and therefore preserves every checked polynomial identity.

For a conditional constructor with numerator event \(A\cap H\) and context event \(H\), the certificate argument gives
\[
 P_{M^s}(H)>0.
\tag{8}
\]
The quotient is therefore defined, and the definition of conditional probability gives
\[
 P_{M^s}(A\mid H)
 =\frac{P_{M^s}(A\cap H)}{P_{M^s}(H)}.
\tag{9}
\]
Equations (2), (6), (7), and (9), by structural induction over the finite trace syntax in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), identify the semantic value of every subexpression of \(\tau\).

Let \(L_\tau\) and \(R_\tau\) be the resulting response-profile expressions at the input and output of the trace, and let \(H_1,\ldots,H_J\) be its distinct divisor expressions. Clearing denominators uses a multiplier
\[
 \Delta_\tau(x)=\prod_{j=1}^{J}H_j(x)^{k_j},
 \qquad k_j\in\mathbb N_{>0},
\tag{10}
\]
with the empty product interpreted as one. By (8),
\[
 \Delta_\tau(x(\mathbf M))>0.
\tag{11}
\]
Acceptance of \(\tau\), by the exact-checker clause of \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), means that rational normalization and coefficient comparison verify the formal polynomial identity
\[
 \Delta_\tau L_\tau-\Delta_\tau R_\tau=0.
\tag{12}
\]
All coordinate sets and sums are finite, so substitution of the response-law coordinates \(x(\mathbf M)\) into (12) is valid and yields
\[
 \Delta_\tau(x(\mathbf M))L_\tau(x(\mathbf M))
 =\Delta_\tau(x(\mathbf M))R_\tau(x(\mathbf M)).
\]
Division by the strictly positive quantity in (11) proves
\[
 L_\tau(x(\mathbf M))=R_\tau(x(\mathbf M)).
\]
Since \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) was arbitrary, every accepted finite fixing trace preserves its represented event probability throughout the compatibility fiber, as claimed.

statements.statement:
Every checked derivation \(\delta:A\Downarrow F\) in the finite extraction calculus satisfies
\[
F(\mathcal P)=P_{M^s}(A)
\]
for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  Every accepted positivity certificate is valid on its declared compatibility fiber.  Moreover, \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(A)\) terminates and accepts if and only if the recursive indicator of \(A\) is independent of the nonfocal response profiles; upon acceptance its constructed row \(\operatorname{row}_D(A)\) equals that indicator for every nonfocal profile.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a domain label \(s\), a checked derivation \(\delta:A\Downarrow F\), and \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). We first prove the positivity assertion needed by quotient nodes. For any accepted positivity certificate, let \(x\) be its finite vector of response-law coordinates and write the checked description of its declared compatibility fiber as
\[
 h_i(x)=0\quad(1\le i\le r),
 \qquad
 g_j(x)\ge 0\quad(1\le j\le t).
\tag{13}
\]
The typing clause of \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\) ensures that the coordinates of every model in the declared fiber satisfy (13). An accepted rational-constant certificate exactly verifies \(p(x)\ge\varepsilon\) with \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q\) and \(\varepsilon>0\). An accepted linear face certificate exactly verifies
\[
 p(x)-\varepsilon
 =\sum_{i=1}^{r}\alpha_i h_i(x)
  +\sum_{j=1}^{t}\lambda_j g_j(x),
 \qquad \varepsilon>0,\quad\lambda_j\ge 0,
\tag{14}
\]
and an accepted preordering certificate exactly verifies
\[
 p(x)-\varepsilon
 =\sum_{i=1}^{r}\tau_i(x)h_i(x)
  +\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}
    \sigma_J(x)\prod_{j\in J}g_j(x),
 \qquad \varepsilon>0,
\tag{15}
\]
where each \(\sigma_J\) is exactly checked to be a finite sum of squares of rational polynomials. On (13), the equality terms in (14) and (15) vanish, all remaining factors are nonnegative, and sums of squares are nonnegative. Therefore every admitted constructor gives
\[
 p(x)\ge\varepsilon>0.
\tag{16}
\]
Exact coefficient comparison establishes (14) and (15) as polynomial identities, so substitution of model coordinates cannot invalidate them. Since these cases exhaust the admitted positivity-certificate grammar, every accepted positivity certificate is valid on its declared compatibility fiber.

We now prove
\[
 F(\mathcal P)=P_{M^s}(A)
\tag{17}
\]
by structural induction on the finite derivation tree in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\). At a supplied-cell leaf, descriptor \(a\) declares a finite primitive tuple \(T_a\), a deterministic finite map \(f_a\), and the returned output \(f_a(T_a)\). By \(\mathrm{ass:typed\text{-}menu\text{-}realizability}\), together with the descriptor semantics in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), its supplied law is the pushforward
\[
 P_a^s=(f_a)_\#\operatorname{Law}_{M^s}(T_a).
\tag{18}
\]
Consequently, for each declared output cell \(y\), the leaf generator has the direct semantics
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)(\mathcal P)
 &=P_a^s(y)\\
 &=\operatorname{Law}_{M^s}\!\bigl(f_a(T_a)\bigr)(y)\\
 &=P_{M^s}\!\bigl(f_a(T_a)=y\bigr).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{19}
\]
This uses the supplied output law itself. The deterministic preimage equality
\[
 \mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
 =\sum_{t:\,f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\}
\tag{20}
\]
is used only to evaluate event indicators, locality truth tables, and response-profile polynomials. In particular, (20) does not make any probability \(P_{M^s}(T_a=t)\) a supplied menu generator. Such a tuple-cell probability is directly available only if the menu separately contains an identity-output descriptor. This proves the induction claim for every supplied leaf without enlarging \(\mathcal P\). Since the deterministic map \(f_a\) is evaluated after \(T_a\) is returned, this evaluation visits no additional structural parent configuration; the carrier in \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}response\text{-}profile}\) therefore suffices for (20).

The contradiction and sure-event leaves have probabilities zero and one. If the induction claim holds for \(A_0\), finite complementarity gives
\[
 P_{M^s}(A_0^{\mathsf c})
 =1-P_{M^s}(A_0)
 =1-F_0(\mathcal P).
\tag{21}
\]
If it holds for a finite pairwise-disjoint family \((A_j:j\in J)\), finite additivity gives
\[
 P_{M^s}\!\left(\bigsqcup_{j\in J}A_j\right)
 =\sum_{j\in J}P_{M^s}(A_j)
 =\sum_{j\in J}F_j(\mathcal P).
\tag{22}
\]
The Boolean-normalization constructor forms a finite disjoint truth-table partition, so (21)--(22) prove its case. A marginalization constructor enumerates the finite partition indexed by the marginalized variable's declared nonempty state space and is another application of (22).

For a fixing constructor, the derivation contains an accepted fixing trace and type-correct substitutions for its leaves. By \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}fixing\text{-}calculus\text{-}soundness}\), the trace preserves the represented event probability. Equations (19), (21), and (22), together with the induction hypotheses, identify the semantic values of all substituted leaves, while type-correct substitution preserves rational constants, finite sums, differences, and products. Thus the fixing constructor preserves (17).

An internal kernel quotient is admitted only after checked derivations of its numerator event \(A_0\cap H\) and context event \(H\), together with an independently accepted strict-positivity certificate for that context. The induction hypotheses and (16) give
\[
 F_H(\mathcal P)=P_{M^s}(H)>0.
\tag{23}
\]
Division is therefore legitimate, and the definition of conditional probability yields
\[
 \frac{F_{A_0\cap H}(\mathcal P)}{F_H(\mathcal P)}
 =\frac{P_{M^s}(A_0\cap H)}{P_{M^s}(H)}
 =P_{M^s}(A_0\mid H).
\tag{24}
\]
There is no unguarded division constructor. The supplied-cell, constant, Boolean-normalization, marginalization, fixing, and certified-quotient cases exhaust the checked derivation grammar. This completes the induction and proves (17).

It remains to prove the assertion about \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\). Fix \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) and define
\[
 \Omega_{-D}
 =\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'},
\tag{25}
\]
where an empty product is a singleton. By \(\mathrm{ass:recursive\text{-}compatibility}\) and \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}response\text{-}profile}\), every factor is finite and recursive evaluation is total. Hence \(A\) has a deterministic indicator
\[
 I_A:\Omega_D\times\Omega_{-D}\longrightarrow\{0,1\}.
\tag{26}
\]
By the exhaustive-checker clause of \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(A)\) compares
\[
 I_A(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})
 =I_A(\omega_D,\omega'_{-D})
\tag{27}
\]
for every \(\omega_D\in\Omega_D\) and every \(\omega_{-D},\omega'_{-D}\in\Omega_{-D}\). The enumerated set is finite, so the checker terminates. If it accepts, all equalities (27) hold, which is exactly independence of the recursive indicator from the nonfocal response profiles. Conversely, that independence makes every equality (27) true, so the exhaustive checker accepts.

Upon acceptance, let \(\omega_{-D}^{0}\) be the checker's fixed reference profile. Its constructed row is
\[
 \operatorname{row}_D(A)(\omega_D)
 =I_A(\omega_D,\omega_{-D}^{0}).
\tag{28}
\]
Combining (27) and (28) gives, for every \(\omega_D\in\Omega_D\) and every \(\omega_{-D}\in\Omega_{-D}\),
\[
 \operatorname{row}_D(A)(\omega_D)
 =I_A(\omega_D,\omega_{-D}).
\]
If the checker rejects, its first failed comparison in the fixed finite enumeration supplies an explicit triple \((\omega_D,\omega_{-D},\omega'_{-D})\) witnessing dependence on the nonfocal profile. This proves termination, the if-and-only-if acceptance characterization, and correctness of the row constructed upon acceptance.

statements.statement:
Assume that the exact global acquisition instance of \(\mathrm{def:global\text{-}regime\text{-}block\text{-}acquisition}\) is admissible.  Then \(\Lambda_S\ne\varnothing\) for every \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\).  The closed evidence test on \(\Lambda_{\varnothing}\) returns uniform zero evidence or mixed zero and positive evidence exactly in those two cases and then defines no arm-ranking acquisition problem.  In the remaining case there is a number \(\epsilon>0\) such that
\[
\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star)\geq\epsilon
\qquad
\text{for every }S\subseteq\mathcal U\text{ and }\vartheta\in\Lambda_S.
\]
In this uniformly positive case the following conclusions hold.

First, for each \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\) and \(\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), membership \(\rho\in\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\) is decided exactly by one closed existential formula over the reals.  Exhaustive enumeration returns every minimum-cost solution of the global acquisition problem using at most
\[
2^{|\mathcal U|}|\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}|
\]
membership quantifier-elimination calls, in addition to a fixed number of evidence calls and one joint-realizability call.

Second, for every \(S\), \(\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\) is exactly the set of arms that are conditionally optimal in at least one original-alphabet SCM family in \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P_S)\).  Thus this acquisition problem is exact for every finite sparse ADMG, not merely for a district-saturated relaxation.

Third, whenever the same augmented information is represented by the local row system, broad compatibility implies
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\subseteq\operatorname{PO}(S).
\]
If, for that augmented menu, the checked arm events are focal-district local and the focal projection hypotheses of \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}district\text{-}fiber\text{-}projection}\) hold, then equality holds.  Hence the local program is always an outer pruning relaxation and is exact only under those additional hypotheses.

Finally, the two-experiment Boolean-pushforward instance of \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}layer3\text{-}acquisition\text{-}obstruction}\) satisfies, in the induced response-law coordinates,
\[
\{q_D^\star(\vartheta):\vartheta\in\Lambda_S\}=\mathcal K_S
\qquad(S\subseteq\{e_1,e_2\}).
\]
Consequently its displayed possibly-optimal table also holds with \(\operatorname{PO}_G\), so \(f_G\) is not submodular in general and the unique exact broad-model acquisition solution in that instance buys both experiments at total cost two.
statements.justification: This theorem makes the sparse-ADMG acquisition layer exact over the broad original-alphabet compatibility fiber while retaining the local row-face problem as a cheaper outer relaxation.
statements.gap: Existing transported-bandit and Layer-3 identification results do not give an exact finite-menu acquisition objective over heterogeneous sparse-ADMG canonical fibers with uniform evidence screening.
statements.consumer: Exact quantifier elimination decides which arms can still be optimal after each candidate regime block and exhaustively returns every least-cost block set achieving full-menu pruning.
statements.proof_tex:
Because \(\mathcal P_S\) contains a subset of the complete cell equations in \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal U}\), Definition \(\mathrm{def:exact\text{-}global\text{-}canonical\text{-}fiber}\) gives
\[
\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\subseteq\Lambda_S\subseteq\Lambda_{\varnothing}
\qquad(S\subseteq\mathcal U).
\tag{1}
\]
Admissibility gives \(\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\ne\varnothing\), so every set in \((1)\) is nonempty.  Each is a closed subset of the finite canonical parameter space and is therefore compact; its defining equalities and inequalities are finite polynomial sign conditions.

Apply the reusable test in Definition \(\mathrm{def:hybrid\text{-}result\text{-}grammar}\) to \(\Lambda_{\varnothing}\).  The quantifier-elimination lemma makes its three closed formulas exactly decidable over \(\mathbb R\).  Since evidence probabilities are nonnegative and the fiber is nonempty, the three cases are exhaustive and disjoint.  In the first two, respectively all evidence probabilities vanish or a zero-evidence point and a positive-evidence point coexist, so a conditional ranking on the entire base fiber is not defined.  In the remaining case the continuous polynomial
\[
e(\vartheta)=\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star)
\]
is strictly positive on the compact set \(\Lambda_{\varnothing}\).  Therefore it attains a minimum
\[
\epsilon=\min_{\vartheta\in\Lambda_{\varnothing}}e(\vartheta)>0.
\tag{2}
\]
The second inclusion in \((1)\) proves the displayed common lower bound on every augmented fiber.

Fix \(S\) and \(\rho\).  By definition,
\[
\rho\in\operatorname{PO}_G(S)
\Longleftrightarrow
\exists\vartheta\left[
\vartheta\in\Lambda_S\ \wedge\
\bigwedge_{\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}}
\{n_\rho(\vartheta)-n_\sigma(\vartheta)\geq0\}
\right].
\tag{3}
\]
The parameter-space constraints, all complete augmented-menu equations, and every numerator in \((3)\) are polynomials with coefficients in the effective ordered ring generated by the disclosed rational or real-algebraic probabilities.  Formula \((3)\) is therefore one closed existential formula in the language of real-closed fields.  The quantifier-elimination lemma returns an equivalent quantifier-free sentence, and exact sign comparison evaluates it.  There are \(2^{|\mathcal U|}\) subsets and \(|\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}|\) arms, proving the stated membership-call bound.  One further existential sentence checks \(\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\ne\varnothing\); the evidence block uses a fixed number of closed calls.  After all memberships are known, finite exact comparison computes \(\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\), tests equality with \(\operatorname{PO}_G(\mathcal U)\), sums the positive effectively comparable costs, and retains every feasible subset having the least cost.  This proves termination and the minimum-cost characterization.

For exact causal meaning, Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:exact\text{-}global\text{-}canonical\text{-}frontier}\), applied to the complete augmented menu \(\mathcal P_S\), gives joint range equality for the finite collection
\[
\{B_\tau\cap E:\tau\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\}\cup\{E\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus every \(\vartheta\in\Lambda_S\) has an original-alphabet family in \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P_S)\) with the same entire vector in \((4)\), and conversely.  By \((2)\), for any two arms,
\[
\frac{n_\rho(\vartheta)}{e(\vartheta)}
\geq
\frac{n_\sigma(\vartheta)}{e(\vartheta)}
\Longleftrightarrow
n_\rho(\vartheta)-n_\sigma(\vartheta)\geq0.
\tag{5}
\]
Joint range equality and \((5)\) prove that \(\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\) is exactly the set of arms conditionally optimal at some broad compatible original-alphabet SCM family.

Now suppose the augmented laws are also represented in a focal row system.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:district\text{-}cell\text{-}linearity}\) sends the focal response law of every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P_S)\) into \(\mathcal K_S\), while the accepted local arm traces send the numerator events to the rows \(n_{\tau,D}\).  Therefore a broad witness for membership in \(\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\) supplies a feasible \(q\in\mathcal K_S\) satisfying every local numerator inequality, which proves
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\subseteq\operatorname{PO}(S).
\tag{6}
\]
Under the augmented focal-projection hypotheses, Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}district\text{-}fiber\text{-}projection}\) gives the reverse realization: every \(q\in\mathcal K_S\) is induced by a family in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P_S)\subseteq\mathcal C(\mathcal P_S)\).  The same local numerator equations then turn every local possibly-optimal witness into a broad witness.  This reverses \((6)\) and proves equality.  Without that projection theorem only \((6)\) has been used.

For the final assertion, use the explicit four-profile instance and the complete Boolean output laws proved in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}layer3\text{-}acquisition\text{-}obstruction}\).  The treatment is intervened upon in every displayed tuple cell, so all supplied cells and arm numerators depend on the canonical family only through the four-point response law \(q\) of \((Y_0,Y_1)\).  Conversely, every \(q\) in each displayed face is an allowed finite response law for that district on the original binary alphabets; choose the remaining root response block deterministically.  Hence, for every subset \(S\),
\[
\{q_D^\star(\vartheta):\vartheta\in\Lambda_S\}=\mathcal K_S.
\tag{7}
\]
Equations \((4)\)--\((5)\) in that theorem and \((7)\) give
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(\varnothing)
=\operatorname{PO}_G(\{e_1\})
=\operatorname{PO}_G(\{e_2\})=\{\rho,\sigma\},
\qquad
\operatorname{PO}_G(\{e_1,e_2\})=\{\sigma\}.
\]
Thus the marginal gain of \(e_2\) is zero at the empty set and one after \(e_1\), so \(f_G\) violates diminishing returns.  Both experiments are necessary and sufficient, giving the stated unique solution and cost.

sampling_model.design: Exact population laws from finite source-labelled menus of observational, hard-interventional, and declared realizable partial-copy regimes.
sampling_model.units: Each law is generated by independent units from its domain-specific finite recursive SCM; identification is at the population-law level.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatments and partial-copy operations are fixed by descriptor \(a\), and source shifts are encoded by \(\Delta_s\).
sampling_model.overlap: No blanket positivity assumption is imposed. The recursion returns \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) for an identified zero evidence probability, and arm-order theorems explicitly restrict to a face on which the common evidence row is positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance estimator enters the identification claim; finite-sample estimation of returned functionals and dual margins is downstream.

estimand_functional: The exact broad conditional range is \(\left[\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)/\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),\ \max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)/\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)\right]\) when \(\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)>0\), for \((\Lambda,\Xi)\in\{(\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\}\).  The QE syntax is computed over the effective coefficient ring and interpreted over \(\mathbb R\).  For global acquisition, \(\Lambda_S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P_S)\), \(\operatorname{PO}_G(S)=\{\rho:\exists\vartheta\in\Lambda_S,\ n_\rho(\vartheta)\geq n_\sigma(\vartheta)\ \text{ for every }\sigma\}\), and the exact design minimizes \(\sum_{e\in S}c_e\) subject to \(\operatorname{PO}_G(S)=\operatorname{PO}_G(\mathcal U)\).  Locally, \(R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}=\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^{\perp}\), and the LP dominance and acquisition maps are exact only under focal saturation plus \(\mathsf{BASep}_D\) or its stated stronger sufficient checks; otherwise they are outer relaxations of the broad canonical program.

tldr: Heterogeneous sites can supply genuine Layer-3 partial-copy laws. A certified extraction judgment turns each available context and cell into a typed district row only after source admissibility is proved. On a fixed-alphabet one-district compatibility face, the sharp transported arm-gap equals an explicit dual weighting of all retained source-labelled cells, and an added Layer-3 regime block yields a finite piecewise-affine pruning frontier. DCTFTR is an inductive, terminating transition system with typed failures and zero-evidence rejection. A complete binary instance gives the margin \(2p-1/2\), while minimum-cost regime-block acquisition and multi-district face preservation remain explicit open questions.

project_justification.gap: CTFTR transports conditional counterfactuals from heterogeneous Layer-1/2 inputs, CTFIDU+ identifies from Layer-3 inputs in one causal specification, and Park--Lee pruning uses graph-based action classes or fixed transported bounds. None derives an exact source-menu certificate or a sign-regime boundary for the order of conditional Layer-3 arms.
project_justification.niche: District-closed shifts and common-evidence arm comparisons reduce one confounded target block to a boundary-sensitive response polytope. Its LP dual converts released source cells into an auditable ranking certificate, while a candidate menu value parametrizes a genuine pruning phase transition.
project_justification.fill: The project proves fixed-alphabet realization of the compatible face, gives certified typed extraction and an inductive DCTFTR semantics, replaces global row span by an active-face criterion, derives sharp primal--dual arm-order certificates, verifies the complete binary phase boundary, and poses minimum-cost regime-block acquisition before asking whether the construction survives multi-district gluing.

related_work: Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim (2022, Theorem 5.1) supply the source-labelled conditional transport architecture for Layers 1 and 2; Proposition 1 proves proper typed inclusion of their problem-instance subgrammar and sound semantic agreement of successful functionals, without asserting syntactic or transition-level equivalence. Raghavan and Bareinboim (2026, Theorem 3.5 and Appendix E.1) supply Layer-3 factor extraction and ctf-thickets for one causal specification; Proposition 1 embeds that setting through \(\mathcal S=\{\star\}\) and proves non-representability of the complete binary multi-domain instance, without claiming that its scalar cell alone is outside CTFIDU+. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022, Theorem 2.4) supply the finite response carrier, and Choe et al. (2026, Proposition 3.1) motivate preserving all information rows; both inform rather than serve as tightening targets. Bareinboim and Pearl (2012, Theorems 5--7) and Bareinboim and Pearl (2014) supply vertex-level selection diagrams and multi-environment completeness, whereas district joint-kernel invariance is a stronger Layer-3 transport condition. Park and Lee (2026, ICLR, Theorems 1--3) define realizable Layer-3 action classes, and Park and Lee (2026, UAI, Theorems 1--2) give valid Layer-1/2 transported bandit bounds; they inform the menu-dual order certificate, binary pruning boundary, and ex-post block-acquisition question rather than serving as results claimed to be beaten.
technical_internal_limitation: Boundary fibers require the active normals \(e_\omega\) for \(\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\); ordinary row span alone can miss identification when the menu forces response profiles to zero. Multi-district completeness is not asserted. The smallest binary two-hedge thicket must compare every recursive failure with target-score constancy on the exact global compatibility fiber; a failed recursion with a constant target would redirect the global claim to sharp polynomial transported bounds.
honest_scope: The face projection, active-face identification criterion, dual arm-order theorem, one-cell phase diagram, and complete binary check concern a reduced one-district comparison with common positive evidence. DCTFTR soundness covers broader district-closed instances, but fixed-cardinality multi-district completeness is open. The acquisition objective is finite and ex post; it is not an ex-ante adaptive policy. No assumption supplies the dominance margin, active face, or threshold. The observational and hard-interventional problem-instance subgrammar is properly included in DCTFTR and successful outputs agree semantically with the target, the one-domain problem-instance class includes the CTFIDU+ setting, and sure evidence reduces conditional arm order to the unconditional numerator-gap program.
